title: Tool-Augmented Agent vs LLM-Only Baseline: Fault-Injected Topology Evaluation (Repaired Preregistration)
research_question: Does augmenting an LLM with a deterministic network verifier and a topology-aware lightweight simulator (tool-augmented agent) increase verifier-pass rates and reduce simulated outage-inducing misconfigurations versus an LLM-only single-shot generator under injected faults and adversarially ambiguous intents?
confirmatory_hypotheses: H1 (primary): The tool-augmented agent yields a higher verifier-pass rate (binary: pass/fail) than the LLM-only pipeline on matched tasks; estimand = paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline (agent − baseline).

H2: The tool-augmented agent yields a lower simulated outage incidence (binary: any destination-pair reachability loss under injected faults) than the LLM-only pipeline (reported as a secondary estimand, exploratory for formal testing).
H3: Relative improvement (verifier-pass rate delta) is larger on complex multi-statement intents than on simple single-statement intents (pre-registered subgroup analysis).
exploratory_questions: E1: Which repair iteration counts dominate improvement (iter=1 vs iter>=2) in the full-agent pipeline?
E2: Typical repair trace patterns and common failure modes (semantic mismatch, parser errors, verifier false-negatives).
E3: Cost trade-offs (model calls, wall-clock latency) required to achieve verifier-pass improvements.
benchmark_scope: Public synthetic topology pool (see sampling_plan) limited to generated topologies and vendor-agnostic CLI templates included in execution artifacts.
Injected fault scenarios (link failures, route flap events) executed only in the lightweight topology simulator described below.
model_scope: Single hosted LLM API (same model used for all pipelines). Model provider and exact model identifier will be recorded in the execution manifest at runtime and included in artifacts; model-call settings are deterministic (temperature=0, top_p=1.0).
transformation_scope: Deterministic config canonicalization: whitespace normalization, vendor-agnostic token mapping, parse-tree canonicalization for verifier/simulator ingestion.
Repair-prompt templates (frozen) that convert verifier diagnostics into constrained edit requests.
primary_estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline on deterministic-verifier pass indicator (agent minus baseline); computed by paired_binary_analysis_v1 executor.
secondary_estimands: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline on simulated outage indicator (agent minus baseline) — reported with CIs and labeled exploratory.
median model-call count difference (agent − baseline) and median wall-clock latency difference (agent − baseline) — cost trade-offs (descriptive).
sampling_plan: Confirmatory sample: 300 intent tasks (paired design). Task strata: 150 simple single-statement intents (ACL single-rule, single-prefix reachability), 150 complex multi-statement intents (BGP policy sequences, multi-prefix policies). Inclusion: public/synthetic topology templates and CLI fragments constructed deterministically from the provided synthetic template pool. Exclusion: tasks that are exact verbatim matches to a public training corpus (auto-detected via exact-string match) will be flagged and removed from the confirmatory set prior to analysis (moved to exploratory). Confirmatory_items=300, Discovery_items=0, task_cluster_count=2. Totals derived: 150 simple + 150 complex = 300 confirmatory tasks.
analysis_plan: Primary analysis: paired_binary_analysis_v1 executor computing paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline on the deterministic-verifier pass indicator, alpha=0.05 two-sided. Primary failed_call_treatment: complete_pair_primary (exclude pairs where either pipeline technical failure prevents a valid binary outcome); sensitivity analysis: complete_pair_primary_with_failure_as_zero_sensitivity (treating failed runs as verifier-fail). Secondary analyses: paired binary estimator on simulated outage indicator (reported with 95% CI, labeled exploratory). Cost comparisons (model-call count, latency) analyzed using nonparametric paired tests (Wilcoxon signed-rank) and descriptive medians/IQR. Stratified subgroup (simple vs complex) interaction tests via Cochran–Mantel–Haenszel; these subgroup tests are pre-registered as secondary/exploratory. All analysis pipeline and exact executor invocation parameters are frozen and recorded in the execution manifest.
multiplicity_plan: Single pre-registered primary endpoint (verifier-pass difference). Secondary and subgroup analyses are labeled exploratory and interpreted without confirmatory multiplicity correction. Sensitivity analyses for failure handling are pre-registered and reported transparently.
missingness_plan: Technical failures (API errors, tool crashes) are logged with provider error codes and timestamps. Primary analysis uses complete-pair handling (exclude pairs lacking both binary outcomes). A sensitivity analysis treats failed model calls as failures (verifier-fail) to bound effects. All exclusions and counts will be reported with reasons and hashes of raw artifacts.

risk_factors: Verbatim task overlap with public corpora or model training data
Simulator/verifier mis-specification causing false-positive verifier passes
detection_procedures: Exact-string matching of each intent and generated config against a curated public-config corpus (automated).
Token-level similarity thresholding (deterministic) to flag near-verbatim matches.
Unit tests that compare verifier outputs on canonical seeded cases to detect semantic drift of verifier or simulator.
item_flagging_rules: If an intent or generated config is an exact match with any public-corpus entry, flag and remove from confirmatory set.
If token-level similarity > 0.95 with a corpus entry, flag for exploratory-only treatment.
contamination_plan.analysis_treatment: Flagged items are excluded from the confirmatory primary analysis and analyzed separately as exploratory. All flags and decisions are deterministically recorded in the execution manifest.
residual_uncertainty: Partial semantic overlap below detection thresholds (non-exact matches) may remain undetected.
Model-side hidden prompts or vendor training data characteristics remain external uncertainties and are noncritical but reported.

budget_scenarios.description: Recommended expected-case: 300 confirmatory tasks; four ablation pipelines (LLM-only, verifier-only, simulator-only, full-agent). Assumes full-agent average model calls per task ≈ 2 (initial + 1 repair on average). Planned_model_calls computed: per-task calls = 1 (LLM-only) +1 (verifier-only) +1 (simulator-only) +2 (full-agent expected) =5; 300*5=1500 planned model calls. Models: ["hosted LLM API (single model, temperature=0)"]; transformations: ["canonicalize CLI formatting","vendor-agnostic token mapping","repair-prompt templates"]. Feasibility rationale: within capability manifest limit (max planned model calls 10000); expected average-case minimizes provider cost while preserving full ablation coverage.
budget_scenarios.feasibility_rationale: Expected-call estimate (1500) fits the hosted-model budget and uses deterministic model settings; simulator/verifier run on CPU-only resources (no local GPU).

budget_scenarios.description: Conservative worst-case: same 300 tasks but full-agent uses up to 3 repair iterations for every task (worst-case model calls). Planned_model_calls computed: per-task calls =1+1+1+4 =7; 300*7=2100 planned calls. This scenario budgets worst-case provider cost and runtime; used if strict no-retry-for-cost policy is unacceptable.
budget_scenarios.feasibility_rationale: Worst-case upper bound still under maximum planned model calls (10000); runtime wall-clock fits within 7-day limit given parallelism limits in hosted API; conservative scenario used only if observed repair rates in pilot runs are high.

power_plan.target_effect: Absolute increase in verifier-pass rate of 0.20 (20 percentage points) is the minimally important effect for operational impact.
power_plan.calculation_method: Normal-approximation for paired-proportion difference and McNemar-compatible paired analysis assumptions; conservative discordant-pair estimate used for sample-size reasoning.
assumptions: Discordant-pair fraction conservatively estimated at 0.30 to account for dependence.
power_plan.minimum_detectable_effect_notes: With n=300 paired tasks and the conservative discordant estimate, the study is powered to detect ~0.20 absolute paired-success difference with >90% power; smaller effects (≈0.10) will have reduced power (~50–70%) and thus are exploratory.
sensitivity_analyses: Recompute power under discordant-pair fractions 0.20 and 0.40 to bound detectable effect sizes.
Report observed discordant counts and the achieved 95% CI for paired difference rather than relying solely on pre-study power.

transformation_families: vendor-agnostic token mapping (canonical tokens for common primitives)
repair-prompt templating (deterministic insertion of verifier diagnostics)
semantic_equivalence_checks: Round-trip parse: original generated config -> parse-tree -> regenerate config -> parse-tree equality.
Reachability-preserving check: NetworkX-based canonical simulator applied to both original and canonicalized configs must produce identical reachability matrices on seed topologies.
Edit-distance thresholding to detect spurious changes introduced by canonicalization.
automatic_rejection_rules: Reject any transformed config whose round-trip parse-tree equality fails.
Reject configs that cannot be parsed deterministically by the canonical parser (parse error).
Reject configs that introduce syntactic constructs outside the pre-registered vendor-agnostic token set.
transformation_validation.audit_sample_policy: Automated deterministic sampling: 10% of confirmatory set (30 tasks) selected via hash-based deterministic sampler; each selected task's transformation artifacts undergo extended automated checks (semantic equivalence and reachability re-run). No manual annotation or review is used; all checks are algorithmic.
transformation_validation.mapping_validation: Mapping tables (token maps) are stored as versioned JSON artifacts and validated by unit tests on canonical examples included in the repository; unit tests are deterministic and included in execution artifacts.
residual_risks: Parser/transformer bugs producing subtle semantic changes undetectable by current checks.
Simulator assumptions (graph-level reachability) may not cover vendor-specific semantic nuances.

remaining_noncritical_uncertainties: Simulator fidelity: lightweight topology/synthetic simulator may not fully capture production forwarding-plane behaviors; this is a bounded external-validity limitation (noncritical) because conclusions are explicitly scoped to the synthetic benchmark.
Single hosted-model scope: using one hosted model limits cross-model generality; this is noncritical because claims are bounded to the tested model and the paper will state this limitation.
Possible undetected semantic overlap with model training data below string-similarity thresholds (contamination detection is deterministic but imperfect).
